coverage.scope: Connect initials, finals and tone marks with the sound of a syllable; pinyin is a reading support, not English spelling.

definition.title: Learn a communication strategy
definition.subtitle: Meet two people
definition.context: Use a few familiar words in a short exchange, then demonstrate understanding of a micro-story.

blocks.text: A pinyin syllable has a final, sometimes an initial, and a tone. Pinyin letters describe Mandarin sounds; read the whole syllable instead of applying English spelling. Listen and compare in the Sound explorer, then close the guide and try the syllables yourself.
Use the existing Sound explorer and Tones teaching demonstrations as the comparison source. These are phonetic practice, not new word meanings.

questions.prompt: Say ma, then ni. Point out the initial and final in each syllable. These are sound demonstrations; you are not being asked to translate them.
questions.context: Use the existing Sound explorer and Tones teaching demonstrations as the comparison source. These are phonetic practice, not new word meanings.
questions.label: Take your speaking turn

rubric.text: I separated the initial from the final without adding an extra vowel.
I used the Mandarin sound examples rather than English letter names.

definition.summary: Your results distinguish checked answers from self-reviewed practice. Unsampled material and unassessed proficiency remain separate.
